subject: business-studies
title: Training & Pay Adventure
welcome_lead: Now you'll compare training methods and pay structures — and calculate wages.
meta_desc: GCSE Business Studies — training methods (induction, on-the-job, off-the-job) and pay structures.
final_note: You can compare training types, identify pay structures and calculate wages from given rates.

concepts.def: Training given to new staff in their first days
Training done at the workplace by doing the job
Training away from the desk (college, course)
% of sales paid as wage to sales staff

walkthroughs.body_html:
Training builds skills and confidence.

Induction: settling in. On-the-job: learn by doing. Off-the-job: external courses, no daily distractions.

Time rate rewards hours not output. Easy to admin. Piece rate drives output but can hurt quality.

Commission motivates sales staff. Bonuses reward hitting targets.

A salesperson earns £1,500 base + 5% commission on £20,000 sales.

Commission = 0.05 × 20,000 = £1,000. Total = £2,500.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a stakeholder and a shareholder?
options: A shareholder owns shares in the company; a stakeholder is anyone affected by or with interest in the business — employees, customers, suppliers, community, plus shareholders.
Stakeholders and shareholders are different spellings of the same word.
Productivity is the number of employees a business has.
Stakeholders are managers and shareholders are workers.
